answer: Each agent opens one kernel record and locks 80 credits in a lotus pool, posting the lock on the ledge for a two-epoch challenge window. Auditors check the funding trail and kernel work log before release; a challenger who proves two records share one operator collects both bonds, and one proven link forfeits the linked cluster, so risk grows with cluster size. Renting a borrowed record fails because the lender cannot answer a fresh challenge without exposing the link. The k-th fake still needs a fresh 80-credit lock, so 1,000 fakes tie up 80,000 credits, while an honest agent locks 80 once.
